title: Event Brand Ambassador at Fleurs de Villes DIANA 2026 in London, UK: Paid Cultural Events Job at Somerset House (£16 Per Hour)
summary: If you are passionate about events, arts, culture, public engagement, and delivering exceptional visitor experiences, the Event Brand Ambassador opportunity with Fleurs de Villes DIANA offers an exciting chance to work at one of London s most prestigious cultural venues. Taking place at the iconic Somerset House in London, this paid placement allows successful applicants to become part of the team delivering the world premiere of Fleurs de Villes DIANA , an extraordinary floral exhibition inspired by the life, humanitarian legacy, and timeless fashion of Diana, Princess of Wales . Running from 16 September to 6 October 2026 , this temporary paid role is ideal for enthusiastic individuals who enjoy interacting with the public, supporting cultural events, and representing purpose-driven organizations. Successful candidates will receive competitive hourly pay while gaining valuable hands-on experience in event operations, customer engagement, and exhibition management. Whether you are looking to strengthen your CV, gain experience in cultural programming, or work alongside internationally recognized organizations, this placement provides a unique opportunity to contribute to an inspiring exhibition celebrating compassion, service, and youth empowerment. About the Event Fleurs de Villes DIANA is a spectacular fresh floral exhibition celebrating the extraordinary life and legacy of Diana, Princess of Wales . Hosted at the historic Somerset House in London, the exhibition features fifteen breathtaking floral mannequins , each designed by some of Britain s leading floral artists. Every floral creation is inspired by one of Princess Diana s most iconic fashion moments while also telling the deeper story behind each appearance. The exhibition goes beyond fashion by highlighting Diana s lasting humanitarian impact, including her work in: HIV/AIDS awareness Humanitarian advocacy International diplomacy Landmine awareness campaigns Charity work Compassionate leadership Global social change One of the exhibition s most powerful themes includes Princess Diana s historic walk through an Angolan minefield, symbolizing courage, compassion, and advocacy for humanitarian causes. Supporting The Diana Award The exhibition is presented in support of The Diana Award , the charity established in memory of Princess Diana. Inspired by her belief that young people have the power to change the world, The Diana Award invests in programmes that empower young leaders and changemakers around the globe. A portion of every ticket sold for the exhibition contributes directly toward supporting these youth empowerment programmes. As an Event Brand Ambassador, successful applicants will represent both: Fleurs de Villes The Diana Award making this role particularly meaningful for individuals who enjoy contributing to socially impactful initiatives. About the Event Brand Ambassador Placement This is a paid placement designed to support the delivery of the exhibition throughout its public opening. Brand Ambassadors will serve as the welcoming face of the exhibition, helping create memorable visitor experiences while ensuring smooth daily operations. Applicants can apply for one of two positions: Weekday position Weekend position The role combines customer service, event operations, public engagement, and cultural interpretation within one of London s most visited heritage venues. Key Responsibilities Successful Event Brand Ambassadors will perform a variety of visitor engagement and operational duties. These include: 1. Welcome Visitors Greet visitors warmly upon arrival. Create a positive first impression. Help visitors feel welcome throughout the exhibition. 2. Represent the Organisations Serve as an ambassador for: Fleurs de Villes The Diana Award while maintaining professionalism and enthusiasm at all times. 3. Provide Exhibition Information Brand Ambassadors will answer visitor questions regarding: The exhibition Floral installations Fleurs de Villes The Diana Award Princess Diana s legacy Comprehensive training and frequently asked questions (FAQs) will be provided before the exhibition begins. 4. Encourage Visitor Participation Staff members will encourage visitors to participate by: Voting for their favourite floral mannequin Learning more about the exhibition s stories Engaging with exhibition features 5. Assist Throughout the Exhibition Rather than remaining in one location, ambassadors will roam across the exhibition to: Support guests Offer assistance Answer questions Improve visitor experiences 6. Manage Visitor Flow During busy periods, ambassadors will: Help reduce congestion Direct visitor movement Maintain an enjoyable exhibition atmosphere 7. Report Operational Issues Event staff will communicate: Visitor feedback Maintenance concerns Operational challenges to the Exhibition Manager. 8. Maintain Exhibition Standards Brand Ambassadors help ensure the exhibition remains: Safe Welcoming Beautifully presented Visitor-friendly Skills and Experience Required Applicants should demonstrate excellent interpersonal and communication skills. Ideal candidates possess: Friendly personality Confidence speaking with the public Excellent communication skills Positive attitude Professional behaviour Enthusiasm Reliability Punctuality Strong customer service mindset Ability to work independently Teamwork skills In addition, applicants should have: An interest in flowers Appreciation for arts and culture Interest in exhibitions Passion for events Understanding of or enthusiasm for The Diana Award s mission Candidates should also be comfortable: Standing for extended periods Walking throughout the exhibition during the workday Working Hours The placement follows a structured daytime schedule. Working hours include: 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM Monday to Friday 30-minute unpaid lunch break Applicants should note that separate weekday and weekend positions are available. Orientation and Training Successful candidates will receive paid training before the exhibition opens. Training consists of: One paid online orientation session One paid in-person orientation session The in-person orientation will take place: Monday, 14 September 2026 at Somerset House. This preparation ensures all Brand Ambassadors feel confident before welcoming visitors. Salary Successful applicants will receive: £16 per hour This competitive hourly rate makes the placement an excellent paid opportunity for individuals seeking experience in the cultural and events sector. What You Will Gain This placement offers numerous professional development benefits. Participants will gain: Professional Event Experience Work on the world premiere of an internationally recognised cultural exhibition. Visitor Engagement Skills Develop practical experience in: Public engagement Customer service Exhibition operations Guest relations Career Development Strengthen your CV with experience at one of London s most prestigious cultural venues. Networking Opportunities Work alongside professionals from: Cultural organisations Event management Visitor services Exhibition production Experience with Purpose-Driven Organisations Represent two internationally recognised organisations committed to culture, education, and youth empowerment. Enhanced Employability Gain transferable skills valued across industries including: Events Tourism Museums Arts administration Hospitality Customer experience Communications Why You Should Apply This placement combines meaningful public engagement with valuable professional experience. Few temporary event roles provide the opportunity to: Work at Somerset House Support an internationally recognised exhibition Celebrate Princess Diana s humanitarian legacy Represent The Diana Award Receive competitive hourly pay Build practical event management skills Strengthen future employment prospects Whether you are pursuing a career in events, arts management, communications, hospitality, public relations, tourism, or customer experience, this placement provides practical experience that employers highly value. Application Deadline Applications close on: Friday, 14 August 2026 at 11:59 PM (BST). Applicants are encouraged to submit their applications well before the deadline to avoid any last-minute technical issues. APPLY HERE How to Apply Interested applicants should complete the official Fleurs de Villes DIANA Job Application Form before the application deadline. Ensure that your application accurately demonstrates your communication skills, enthusiasm for visitor engagement, professionalism, and interest in cultural events. Visit HERE for more information about the Event Brand Ambassador opportunity at Fleurs de Villes DIANA 2026 in London, UK. Conclusion The Event Brand Ambassador placement for Fleurs de Villes DIANA presents a rare opportunity to become part of a landmark international cultural exhibition while earning competitive pay. Hosted at Somerset House in London, this role allows participants to develop practical experience in event operations, customer engagement, and public-facing communications while representing two organizations dedicated to culture, compassion, and youth empowerment. With paid training, valuable networking opportunities, and the chance to strengthen your CV through real-world experience, this placement is an excellent stepping stone for anyone interested in the events, arts, tourism, or cultural sectors. title: Tandem Youth Voice Fellowship 2026–2027 in the USA: Fully Remote Paid Youth Leadership Program for High School Students (Scholarship Included)
summary: The In Tandem Youth Voice Fellowship 2026–2027 is now accepting applications from eligible high school students across the United States who are passionate about making their voices heard and influencing the products, services, and programs that directly affect young people. Designed as a fully remote, year-round fellowship , this unique opportunity empowers teenagers to collaborate with organizations, researchers, and designers while developing practical leadership, research, communication, and design-thinking skills. Unlike many youth programs that prioritize academic excellence or extensive extracurricular achievements, the In Tandem Youth Voice Fellowship focuses on creating opportunities for motivated young people regardless of GPA, previous work experience, or professional background. Participants become Youth Partners who contribute valuable insights through interviews, surveys, focus groups, and collaborative design projects that help organizations better understand the needs and experiences of young people. The fellowship also ensures accessibility by providing computers and internet access to participants who may lack reliable technology, making it possible for more students to participate regardless of their economic background. If you are a high school student looking for a meaningful opportunity to build your resume, gain real-world experience, connect with peers nationwide, and receive financial compensation for your contributions, this fellowship could be an ideal opportunity. About the In Tandem Youth Voice Fellowship The In Tandem Youth Voice Fellowship is a year-round youth engagement initiative that brings together teenagers from across the United States to collaborate with companies, nonprofit organizations, researchers, and design teams. Rather than simply studying youth experiences, In Tandem places young people directly at the center of research and innovation by giving them opportunities to share their perspectives and influence real-world decision-making. Throughout the fellowship, Youth Partners participate remotely in structured research and design activities that explore issues affecting teenagers today. Their opinions help organizations improve products, services, educational programs, healthcare initiatives, community projects, and other youth-focused solutions. The program combines: Behavioral science User-centered design Youth research Leadership development Peer collaboration Professional mentorship Participants work within a structured environment that values youth voices while teaching practical skills that can benefit them throughout high school, college, and future careers. Purpose of the Fellowship The fellowship aims to ensure that young people actively participate in shaping decisions that influence their lives. Instead of adults making assumptions about teenage experiences, organizations work directly with Youth Partners to understand: Youth perspectives Everyday challenges Behavioral patterns Educational experiences Technology usage Product preferences Community needs Social issues affecting teenagers By involving young people throughout the research process, organizations create more inclusive and effective programs while students gain invaluable professional experience. What Participants Will Do Throughout the fellowship, Youth Partners participate in various research and design activities designed to improve youth-centered products and services. These activities include: Participating in interviews Completing research surveys Joining focus group discussions Testing ideas and concepts Providing user feedback Sharing lived experiences Contributing to research studies Helping improve youth-focused products Working alongside professional research teams Supporting human-centered design projects Every activity contributes toward helping organizations understand what young people truly need and value. Fellowship Benefits Participants receive a wide range of professional, educational, and personal development opportunities throughout the program. 1. Work on Real-World Projects Youth Partners collaborate with companies and organizations conducting authentic research projects. Rather than completing classroom exercises, participants contribute directly to projects that may influence future products and services designed for young people. 2. Develop Research Skills Participants learn professional research methods including: Survey development Interview participation Focus group engagement Data collection User feedback techniques Human-centered research These skills are increasingly valuable across numerous academic and career fields. 3. Build Design Thinking Skills The fellowship introduces participants to design thinking principles that emphasize: Problem-solving Creativity Empathy Innovation User-centered design Critical thinking These competencies are useful in higher education and future employment. 4. Learn Behavioral Science Students receive an introduction to behavioral science concepts, helping them understand: Human behavior Decision-making User experiences Research ethics Scientific observation This exposure provides an excellent foundation for students interested in psychology, sociology, public policy, healthcare, marketing, or research careers. 5. Network with Peers Nationwide Participants join a community of Youth Partners from across the United States. Networking opportunities include: Virtual events Development workshops Collaborative activities Team discussions Peer learning experiences Students build friendships while expanding their professional networks. 6. Learn from Industry Professionals The fellowship provides direct engagement with experienced professionals, including: Product designers Researchers Design teams Behavioral scientists Program leaders These interactions expose participants to careers they may not have previously considered. 7. Receive Financial Compensation One of the fellowship s standout benefits is that participants are compensated through a scholarship for their contributions. Students are rewarded for the time, effort, and expertise they bring to research activities, making this both a learning opportunity and a paid experience. 8. Technology Support Recognizing that technology access should never be a barrier, In Tandem provides: Computers when needed Internet access support for eligible participants This commitment ensures equal participation opportunities. Program Structure The fellowship consists of several interconnected components designed to support participants throughout the year. Youth Partners Youth Partners participate in: Research projects Surveys Interviews Focus groups Virtual networking Collaborative learning experiences Their primary responsibility is sharing authentic youth perspectives that inform organizational decision-making. Peer Mentors Experienced Youth Partners may become Peer Mentors. Peer Mentors: Support newer participants Facilitate group activities Participate in quarterly events Share experiences Strengthen leadership abilities This role offers additional leadership development opportunities. Virtual Summer Orientation The fellowship begins with a comprehensive virtual summer orientation lasting approximately one week. During orientation, participants learn: Behavioral science fundamentals Teen research methods User-centered design Design thinking Scientific method Feedback techniques Program expectations Students also meet fellow participants and begin building relationships before engaging in research projects. Time Commitment The fellowship operates throughout the year. Participants engage in research activities and virtual events according to the program schedule. Specific time commitments are discussed with accepted participants to ensure expectations remain manageable alongside school responsibilities. Why This Fellowship Stands Out Unlike many competitive youth programs, the In Tandem Youth Voice Fellowship emphasizes potential rather than academic credentials. There are: No GPA requirements No extracurricular requirements No professional experience requirements No previous research experience required Instead, the fellowship seeks students willing to participate, collaborate, learn, and share honest perspectives. This makes the opportunity significantly more accessible to students from diverse backgrounds. Safety and Privacy In Tandem emphasizes youth safety and participant privacy throughout the fellowship. The organization has dedicated policies and procedures designed to protect participants while maintaining a safe virtual learning environment. Parents and students can review the organization s youth safety and privacy information before participation. Who Should Apply? This fellowship is ideal for students who: Want their voices to influence real-world decisions Enjoy sharing ideas Are interested in research Want to build leadership skills Like collaborating with peers Want professional experience before college Are curious about behavioral science Wish to learn design thinking Want to strengthen communication skills Want to earn compensation while learning Application Process The application process is designed to be straightforward. Applicants should expect the application to take approximately 30 minutes to complete. Students are encouraged to answer questions thoughtfully and honestly, highlighting their perspectives and interest in contributing to youth-centered research. APPLY HERE Application Deadline Applications close on Wednesday, August 19, 2026, at 11:59 PM EST. Applicants are strongly encouraged to submit their applications well before the deadline to avoid last-minute technical issues. Visit HERE for more information about the Tandem Youth Voice Fellowship 2026–2027 in the USA, Conclusion The In Tandem Youth Voice Fellowship 2026–2027 offers an outstanding opportunity for high school students to participate in meaningful research while developing professional skills that extend far beyond the classroom. Through collaboration with experienced researchers, product designers, and organizations, participants gain valuable experience in behavioral science, design thinking, communication, and leadership. The fellowship s inclusive application process, remote format, technology support, and scholarship compensation make it accessible to students from a wide range of backgrounds. For teenagers eager to influence real-world decisions, expand their professional network, and prepare for future academic and career success, this fellowship represents an exceptional opportunity worth pursuing before the application deadline. title: Global Model FAO 2026 Registration Opens: Join Future Leaders at the FAO Headquarters in Rome

Hosted at the headquarters of the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) in Rome, Italy, this prestigious international event provides participants with a unique opportunity to experience how international negotiations are conducted within one of the world s leading United Nations agencies. Global Model FAO 2026 offers participants an immersive diplomatic experience where they will represent countries, debate pressing global issues, negotiate policies, and collaborate with delegates from different regions of the world. The conference aims to strengthen participants understanding of international cooperation while developing practical leadership, communication, negotiation, and policy-making skills. Whether you are participating as a student delegate, faculty advisor, or observer, Global Model FAO 2026 provides an outstanding platform for learning, networking, and professional development. What is Global Model FAO? Global Model FAO is an international simulation of the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations. During the conference, participants assume the role of ambassadors and country representatives, engaging in discussions and negotiations on issues affecting agriculture, food systems, rural development, climate resilience, nutrition, and global food security. Rather than simply observing international diplomacy, participants actively engage in committee sessions that mirror real FAO negotiations. This practical learning experience enables attendees to gain valuable insight into how international organizations work to address global challenges. Why Participate in Global Model FAO 2026? Participating in Global Model FAO offers much more than attending a conference. It is an opportunity to build practical diplomatic experience while connecting with participants from diverse academic and cultural backgrounds. Participants will have the opportunity to: Experience realistic United Nations negotiations. Represent a country during committee sessions. Strengthen diplomacy and public speaking skills. Improve negotiation and consensus-building abilities. Develop leadership and teamwork competencies. Learn about international food security and sustainable agriculture policies. title: AI for SDGs Global Youth AI Future Innovation Competition 2026: International AI Competition for Innovative Solutions Transforming Education and Advancing Sustainable Development Goals
summary: The AI for SDGs Global Youth AI Future Innovation Competition 2026 is an international science and technology innovation competition designed to empower young innovators, researchers, entrepreneurs, organizations, and technology leaders to use artificial intelligence (AI) to address global challenges and contribute to sustainable development. Initiated by the UNU Global AI Network , the competition provides a global platform for participants to develop, showcase, and scale innovative AI solutions that create positive social impact. The 2026 edition focuses on the theme: “AI and Education: AI Transforming the Educational Paradigm and Enhancing AI Literacy” This theme highlights one of the most important transformations of the modern era: the role of artificial intelligence in reshaping education systems, improving learning experiences, and preparing societies for an AI-driven future. The competition explores two major areas: How AI can transform education systems, teaching methods, and learning experiences. How individuals and communities can develop AI literacy and the skills needed to responsibly use and shape AI technologies. The competition will bring together innovators from around the world to create solutions aligned with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly: SDG 4: Quality Education SDG 9: Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure SDG 10: Reduced Inequalities SDG 17: Partnerships for the Goals Competition Theme: AI and Education Artificial intelligence is rapidly changing how people learn, teach, work, and interact with technology. The 2026 competition encourages participants to explore how AI can create more accessible, inclusive, and effective education systems. Participants are invited to develop solutions that address challenges in education through innovation, technology, and responsible AI implementation. The competition focuses on two major dimensions: 1. AI Transforming Educational Paradigms This track explores how AI can redesign traditional educational models and improve learning systems. Participants can develop AI solutions in areas such as: Personalized learning platforms Intelligent tutoring systems Adaptive learning technologies AI-supported curriculum development AI-generated educational content Automated assessment and feedback systems Predictive analytics for identifying students who need support Educational administration and resource optimization Language learning and translation technologies Inclusive learning solutions for students with disabilities Teacher training and AI-assisted instruction This track supports the advancement of: SDG 4: Quality Education 2. AI for Social Innovation This track focuses on using artificial intelligence to solve social challenges, promote equality, and create inclusive educational opportunities. Projects may focus on: AI-powered platforms improving access to quality education Technologies reducing the digital divide AI solutions supporting lifelong learning Workforce reskilling and professional development platforms Community learning initiatives Digital citizenship and misinformation awareness tools AI solutions supporting gender equality in education Technologies promoting cultural diversity and inclusion Data-driven tools for education policy improvement This track contributes to: SDG 4: Quality Education SDG 5: Gender Equality SDG 10: Reduced Inequalities SDG 16: Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions 3. AI for Less Developed Countries (LDCs) This track encourages the development of affordable and practical AI solutions designed for underserved communities and regions with limited resources. Participants are encouraged to create technologies that improve education access and AI capacity in developing regions. Possible solutions include: Low-cost AI learning tools Offline-capable AI education platforms Mobile-based educational technologies AI solutions for remote communities AI literacy programs for young people and educators Teacher training technologies Context-specific AI educational resources Voice-activated or SMS-based learning systems Local language preservation technologies Community-driven AI education initiatives This track supports: SDG 4: Quality Education SDG 9: Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure SDG 10: Reduced Inequalities Who Can Apply? The AI for SDGs Global Youth AI Future Innovation Competition welcomes participation from innovators worldwide. Eligible applicants include: Individuals Student innovators Youth groups Research teams Startups Companies Technology organizations Social innovation groups There are no nationality restrictions. Applications are open globally regardless of nationality, background, race, ethnicity, or country of residence. Participants from all continents are encouraged to apply. Eligibility Requirements Applicants must meet the following requirements: 1. Global Participation The competition is open to participants worldwide. There are no restrictions based on: Nationality Country Region Ethnic background Professional background 2. Technology Readiness Level Requirement Submitted projects must have reached at least: Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 6 or above This means projects should: Have moved beyond the laboratory stage Be tested or validated in real-world environments Demonstrate practical application potential Show innovation and market possibilities Be close to commercial implementation Projects at advanced stages may include: TRL 7 A system prototype demonstrated in an operational environment. TRL 8 A completed system tested, qualified, and prepared for commercialization. TRL 9 A fully proven system successfully operating in real-world missions or commercial deployment. 3. Enterprise Requirement For projects that have already registered as companies: The company must have been established for fewer than 10 years. 4. Language Requirement The official language of the competition is: English All applications, supporting documents, and evaluations will be conducted in English. 5. Participation Fees The competition is completely free. Participants are not required to pay: Registration fees Training fees Participation fees Competition Timeline The 2026 Global Youth AI Future Innovation Competition will take place through three main stages: Application Period Open Application: Now – September 15, 2026 Participants must submit their applications before the deadline. Initial Judge Round September 16 – September 30, 2026 Conducted mainly online Projects will be reviewed and evaluated by judges Semi-Final Round October 1 – October 15, 2026 Conducted mainly online Selected teams will advance based on project quality, innovation, and impact potential Global Final and Award Ceremony November 26, 2026 Location: Macau SAR, China The final competition and award ceremony will be held offline in Macau. Benefits for Finalists Finalist teams will receive valuable support and opportunities, including: Complimentary hotel accommodation during the global final program in Macau Opportunity to showcase innovative AI solutions internationally Networking opportunities with global innovators, researchers, and organizations Exposure to AI and sustainable development communities Opportunity to apply for limited travel allowances Selected finalist teams may receive travel support of up to: $1,000 USD per team (before tax) Understanding Social Innovation Social innovation refers to the development and application of new ideas, technologies, methods, or approaches to solve important societal challenges. Unlike traditional innovation focused only on commercial success, social innovation aims to create positive social impact. It may involve: Education improvement Environmental sustainability Public policy solutions Social inclusion Community empowerment Cross-sector partnerships Social innovation often involves collaboration between: Governments Businesses Research institutions Communities Non-profit organizations The goal is to create sustainable solutions that improve society. Read More About This Opportunity HERE How to Apply Interested applicants should prepare: A description of their AI innovation project Explanation of the problem being addressed Details of the AI technology used Evidence of innovation and impact Supporting project information Applications must be submitted through the official competition application platform. APPLY HERE Contact Information For additional information about the competition: Email: ai4sdgs@venturecup.cn Why Participate in the AI for SDGs Competition? The AI for SDGs Global Youth AI Future Innovation Competition provides a unique opportunity for innovators to use artificial intelligence to solve real-world challenges. Participants can contribute to the future of education by developing solutions that improve accessibility, inclusion, learning outcomes, and digital skills worldwide. With global recognition, international networking opportunities, and a platform to showcase impactful AI solutions, the competition supports the next generation of technology leaders committed to sustainable development. Conclusion The AI for SDGs Global Youth AI Future Innovation Competition 2026 represents a major opportunity for innovators, entrepreneurs, students, researchers, and organizations to demonstrate how artificial intelligence can transform education and create meaningful social impact. Through its focus on AI-powered education solutions, AI literacy, and inclusive innovation, the competition encourages participants to address some of the world s most pressing challenges while contributing to the Sustainable Development Goals. Eligible participants worldwide are encouraged to submit their innovative AI projects before September 15, 2026 , and become part of a global movement using technology to build a smarter, more inclusive, and sustainable future. title: New York Times Editing Residency 2027–2029: Paid Two-Year Programme for Early-Career Journalists
summary: Applications are now open for the New York Times Editing Residency 2027–2029 , a paid, full-time programme designed to develop the next generation of newsroom editors. The two-year residency combines practical editing experience, structured professional training and rotations across different desks within The New York Times newsroom. Residents will work alongside experienced journalists and editors while strengthening the judgment, clarity, precision and contextual awareness required to shape high-quality journalism. The New York Times plans to select three editing residents , who are expected to join the organisation in late January 2027 . Successful applicants will work full time, receive employee benefits and participate in dedicated training and speaker programmes throughout the residency. The most competitive candidates will have between two and seven years of professional journalism experience , together with a clear commitment to developing the craft of editing. Applications must be submitted by 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time on Tuesday, 8 September 2026 . About the New York Times Editing Residency The New York Times Editing Residency is an early-career professional development programme created to cultivate editors who can help shape the future of journalism. Editing remains one of the most important functions within a newsroom. Editors do far more than correct spelling, grammar or punctuation. They help determine whether a story is accurate, clear, fair, well-structured and appropriately presented for its intended audience. Strong editors must be able to: Exercise sound editorial judgment Identify gaps in reporting Improve clarity and organisation Evaluate context and accuracy Work collaboratively with reporters Protect the integrity of published journalism Adapt stories for different formats and audiences Recognise ethical, legal and reputational concerns The residency reflects the reality that editing continues to change as news organisations increasingly use visual journalism, multimedia storytelling, data, graphics, video, interactive formats and other digital approaches. Residents will therefore enter a newsroom environment in which editing is both a traditional journalistic discipline and an evolving creative practice. Purpose of the Programme The central purpose of the residency is to provide promising journalists with the practical experience, guidance and professional tools needed to become accomplished editors. The programme seeks to develop candidates who can contribute meaningfully to journalism while learning from editors across The New York Times. Its objectives include: Developing the next generation of newsroom editors Strengthening editorial judgment and decision-making Providing practical experience across different newsroom desks Building confidence in editing complex stories Exposing residents to different forms of journalism Supporting professional growth through structured training Creating pathways for candidates from diverse backgrounds Helping residents understand how a major international newsroom operates Rather than placing participants in one narrow role for the entire programme, the residency provides exposure to multiple areas of the newsroom. Residency Duration The New York Times Editing Residency is a two-year, full-time programme covering the 2027–2029 period. The three selected residents are expected to begin working at The Times in late January 2027 . Because this is a full-time professional commitment, applicants should be prepared to participate throughout the entire residency period and carry out the responsibilities associated with their assigned newsroom desks. Desk Rotations Residents will work across a range of desks during the programme. The information provided does not identify the exact desks or specify how long each rotation will last. However, the rotational structure is intended to expose participants to different editorial environments, workflows, subject areas and forms of storytelling. A desk rotation may help residents understand how editorial priorities vary depending on: The type of journalism being produced The subject matter being covered The intended audience The speed of the news cycle The format of the final publication The level of collaboration required The reporting and production resources available Working across multiple desks can also help residents identify their editorial strengths and determine which areas of journalism they may wish to pursue in the future. What Editing Residents Will Gain Practical Newsroom Experience Residents will work inside The New York Times newsroom and contribute to the editorial process on a full-time basis. This practical experience is central to the programme. Participants will not simply observe newsroom operations; they will gain direct exposure to the decisions, responsibilities and collaborative relationships that shape published journalism. Development of Editorial Judgment Editorial judgment involves deciding what information matters, what requires further reporting, what may confuse readers and how a story should be framed or organised. Residents will have opportunities to strengthen their ability to assess: Accuracy Relevance Structure Tone Clarity Context Fairness Reader understanding These skills are difficult to acquire through theory alone. They require repeated practice, feedback and guidance from experienced professionals. Dedicated Training Residents will participate in training programmes created specifically to support their professional development. The announcement does not provide a complete curriculum, but the training is expected to complement residents’ practical work across the newsroom. Training may help participants reflect on their editorial decisions, understand newsroom standards and develop skills that can be applied throughout their careers. Speaker Programmes Editing residents will also attend dedicated speaker programmes at The New York Times. These sessions may provide opportunities to hear from experienced journalists, editors and newsroom leaders about their work, professional development and perspectives on the changing media industry. Exposure to Evolving Storytelling Formats Modern journalism is increasingly produced through combinations of text, images, graphics, video, audio, data and interactive formats. The residency offers participants an opportunity to understand how editing operates within this broader storytelling environment. Editors must increasingly consider not only the words in an article but also how different elements work together to communicate information clearly and responsibly. Professional Network Development Working across desks will allow residents to build relationships with journalists, editors and newsroom leaders. These professional connections may become an important source of mentorship, collaboration and career guidance during and after the programme. Compensation and Benefits The New York Times Editing Residency is a paid programme. Residents will: Work full time Receive compensation Receive employee benefits Participate in dedicated training Attend speaker programmes Gain experience across multiple newsroom desks The available information does not state the exact salary, financial package or individual benefits. Applicants should consult the official application page for complete employment terms. Number of Available Positions The New York Times plans to welcome: Three editing residents Because only three participants are expected to be selected, the application process is likely to be highly competitive. Candidates should ensure that their applications clearly demonstrate both relevant journalism experience and a genuine commitment to editing. Who Should Apply? The programme is intended for early-career and developing journalists who want to strengthen their editorial skills. The most competitive applicants will have: At least two years of professional journalism experience No more than seven years of professional journalism experience A demonstrated commitment to editing Some newsroom editing experience Strong editorial judgment An interest in learning across multiple desks The ability to work collaboratively A commitment to clear and responsible journalism The announcement indicates that candidates with existing newsroom editing experience are likely to be particularly competitive. However, applicants should not view editing only as a formal job title. Journalists may have gained relevant experience by editing colleagues’ work, managing publications, coordinating reporting projects, reviewing scripts or shaping stories for digital and multimedia platforms. Professional Experience Requirement The preferred experience range is: A minimum of two years and a maximum of seven years of professional journalism experience This range suggests that the programme is aimed at journalists who have already gained meaningful professional experience but remain at a relatively early stage in their careers. Applicants with fewer than two years or more than seven years of experience may be less competitive based on the stated criteria. The announcement refers specifically to professional journalism experience. Candidates should therefore clearly document the nature, duration and responsibilities of their journalism work. Commitment to the Craft of Editing A strong application should communicate why the candidate wants to become an editor and how their previous experience has prepared them for the residency. Commitment to editing may be demonstrated through experience such as: Editing reported articles Working on a student or professional publication Providing structural feedback to writers Fact-checking Managing editorial workflows Editing newsletters or digital content Coordinating collaborative reporting Reviewing multimedia scripts Supporting publication standards Working with reporters to strengthen stories Candidates should focus on meaningful examples rather than simply stating that they enjoy writing or journalism. Diversity and Inclusion The New York Times states that it aims to recruit candidates from diverse backgrounds. The goal is to provide participants with the tools and experiences they need to help shape journalism. Diversity may contribute to stronger journalism by expanding the perspectives, experiences and forms of knowledge represented in editorial decision-making. No racial, ethnic, gender or national group is identified as an exclusive eligibility category in the information provided. Selection Process Applications will close on 8 September 2026. After the deadline, the programme directors and editors from across the newsroom will work together to select the residents. The process is expected to assess: Professional journalism experience Editing experience Commitment to editorial work Career potential Ability to contribute to the newsroom Alignment with the programme’s development goals Only three residents are expected to be appointed. The available information does not explain whether shortlisted candidates will complete interviews, assessments or editing exercises. Applicants should therefore review the official application instructions carefully. How to Apply Interested candidates should submit their applications through the official application page. Applicants should follow the instructions on the application platform and provide all requested information and supporting materials. Questions about the programme may be directed to the relevant Early Career Programs team contact identified in the official announcement. APPLY HERE Application Deadline Applications must be submitted by: 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time on Tuesday, 8 September 2026 Late applications may not be considered. Applicants should avoid waiting until the final hours before the deadline, as last-minute technical problems, incomplete uploads or missing information can turn a promising application into a small digital tragedy. Why Apply for the New York Times Editing Residency? The residency offers an unusual combination of professional employment and structured editorial development. Participants will receive: Two years of full-time newsroom experience Paid employment and benefits Rotations across different desks Dedicated editorial training Access to speaker programmes Guidance from experienced editors Exposure to different forms of storytelling Opportunities to build a professional network A chance to contribute to an internationally recognised news organisation For journalists committed to editing, the programme provides an opportunity to deepen their craft while learning how editorial decisions are made in a complex, fast-moving newsroom. Conclusion The New York Times Editing Residency 2027–2029 is a paid, two-year opportunity for developing journalists who want to become stronger editors. Three residents will work full time across multiple newsroom desks, receive benefits and participate in dedicated training and speaker programmes. The residency is designed to strengthen editorial judgment, clarity, contextual understanding and the ability to shape journalism across traditional and evolving storytelling formats. The most competitive candidates will have between two and seven years of professional journalism experience and will demonstrate a clear commitment to editing. Applications close at 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time on 8 September 2026 , and the selected residents are expected to begin working at The New York Times in late January 2027. For further information about this opportunity, CLICK HERE . To discover more job opportunities, VISIT HERE . title: 2027 Movement Leader Fellowship: A Comprehensive Leadership Development Opportunity for Experienced Social Justice Organizers
summary: Applications are now open for the 2027 Movement Leader Fellowship, an intensive seven-month leadership development program designed specifically for experienced social justice organizers seeking to strengthen their strategic leadership skills, deepen their organizational impact, and build sustainable movements for long-term change. Created by Leadership for Democracy and Social Justice, this fellowship combines graduate-level academic learning, leadership coaching, immersive retreats, and peer collaboration to help movement leaders become stronger organizers, better managers, and more effective strategists. Unlike many leadership programs that focus solely on theory, the Movement Leader Fellowship is designed around practical application. Fellows continue working full-time while applying what they learn directly to their organizations, campaigns, and communities throughout the duration of the program. Application Deadlines Applicants should take note of the following important dates: Priority Application Deadline: September 21, 2026 Final Application Deadline: October 19, 2026 Candidates who submit applications before the priority deadline receive priority consideration during the selection process. APPLY HERE For more information, visit HERE Visit OFY Website HERE for more fellowship opportunities About the 2027 Movement Leader Fellowship The Movement Leader Fellowship is a seven-month professional leadership program running from January through July 2027 . It is designed for experienced organizers working within organizations that build political, economic, and social power through grassroots organizing rather than relying primarily on advocacy or direct service. The fellowship helps participants strengthen their leadership by providing structured opportunities to: Develop long-term strategic thinking. Improve organizational leadership. Strengthen campaign strategy. Lead teams more effectively. Build resilient organizations. Sustain themselves personally while carrying demanding leadership responsibilities. Throughout the fellowship, participants remain employed in their current organizations while integrating new leadership tools into their daily work. Fellowship Structure The program combines several learning experiences into one comprehensive leadership journey. Participants will engage in: Graduate-Level Coursework Fellows participate in rigorous academic learning designed to strengthen their understanding of leadership, organizing, movement strategy, organizational development, and systems change. The coursework provides practical frameworks that can immediately be applied to ongoing campaigns and organizational priorities. Leadership Coaching Each fellow receives individualized leadership coaching. Coaching focuses on helping participants: Navigate organizational challenges. Strengthen decision-making. Improve leadership effectiveness. Address complex management responsibilities. Develop long-term leadership strategies. Immersive Retreats Participants attend immersive retreats that provide opportunities for: Intensive leadership development. Reflection. Collaborative learning. Strategic planning. Relationship building with fellow movement leaders. These retreats create dedicated space away from daily organizational responsibilities, allowing fellows to focus deeply on personal and organizational growth. National Community of Leaders The fellowship also creates a national network of experienced organizers. Participants learn alongside peers facing similar leadership challenges, allowing them to: Exchange ideas. Share organizing strategies. Build lasting professional relationships. Collaborate across organizations and movements. Support one another throughout their leadership journeys. Fellowship Duration The fellowship runs over a period of seven months , beginning in January 2027 and concluding in July 2027 . The program has been intentionally designed to fit alongside full-time employment, enabling participants to continue leading within their organizations while completing fellowship requirements. Financial Support The total cost of the fellowship is approximately $27,600 per participant . This amount covers: Tuition Travel expenses Accommodation Meals Course materials Leadership coaching Faculty and instructional support Thanks to funding partners, fellows pay only a small portion of the actual program cost through a shared investment model. Individual Contribution Each participant contributes: $500 This contribution covers participation costs, including travel, tuition, coaching, and other fellowship-related expenses. Applicants who are unable to afford this contribution may request financial assistance. Organizational Contribution Organizations are encouraged to contribute toward the fellowship using a sliding-scale model based on their annual operating budget. Organizations with annual budgets below $2 million Suggested contribution: $2,500 Organizations with annual budgets between $2 million and $5 million Suggested contribution: $4,000 Organizations with annual budgets above $5 million Suggested contribution: $7,500 Organizations with greater financial capacity help make the fellowship accessible to leaders from smaller or under-resourced organizations. Scholarship Support A limited number of scholarships are available for fellows who cannot make any financial contribution. Importantly: Financial need does not affect admissions decisions. Applicants are evaluated independently of their ability to pay. Employers may contribute on behalf of fellows. Selection Process The fellowship follows a structured admissions process. Applicants who submit by the Priority Deadline Applications reviewed first. Interview invitations sent by email. Interviews conducted between late September and early October. Applicants who submit by the Final Deadline Interview invitations sent after application review. Interviews conducted in early November. Final Cohort The fellowship will admit up to 28 fellows . Successful applicants receive invitations by email in early November. Program dates may change if necessary, and applicants will be informed of any updates. Information Sessions Prospective applicants can participate in virtual information sessions before applying. Scheduled sessions include: August 27, 2026 September 15, 2026 October 14, 2026 These sessions provide an opportunity to learn more about the fellowship, ask questions, and better understand the program expectations. Eligibility Criteria Ideal applicants should demonstrate significant leadership experience within organizing movements. Applicants should: Have approximately 10–15 years of experience in social justice leadership. Be committed to long-term movement building. Work within organizations that build power through organizing and member engagement. Be employed full-time. Lead teams, campaigns, budgets, or major organizational initiatives. Be actively developing or leading an important organizational project that can be strengthened throughout the fellowship. Be managing increasingly complex leadership responsibilities. Be deeply connected to historically oppressed communities. Be committed to rigorous learning alongside peers. Be able to participate fully in every component of the fellowship. Why Apply? The Movement Leader Fellowship offers much more than professional development. Participants gain opportunities to: Strengthen strategic leadership skills. Expand organizational management capacity. Learn directly from experienced movement leaders. Receive personalized executive coaching. Build a national network of accomplished organizers. Apply graduate-level learning to real organizational challenges. Develop sustainable leadership practices. Increase long-term impact within movements for social justice. Conclusion The 2027 Movement Leader Fellowship is an outstanding opportunity for experienced organizers seeking to elevate their leadership while continuing their work within social justice movements. Through graduate-level education, personalized coaching, immersive retreats, and collaboration with a national cohort of peers, fellows gain the knowledge, practical tools, and strategic perspective needed to lead stronger organizations and build lasting social change. With substantial financial support covering most program costs, scholarship opportunities for those with financial need, and a flexible structure that accommodates full-time employment, the fellowship represents a significant investment in the next generation of movement leadership. Interested applicants should submit their applications before the Priority Deadline of September 21, 2026 , or no later than the Final Deadline of October 19, 2026 . title: Migration Partnership Facility 2026 Calls for Proposals: Up to €6 Million Available for EU Member States to Strengthen Migration Partnerships, Border Management, and Internal Security
summary: The Migration Partnership Facility (MPF) has officially launched its 2026 Calls for Proposals, offering substantial funding opportunities for European Union Member States to implement strategic migration initiatives with partner countries. Backed by the European Union, the latest funding calls are designed to strengthen international cooperation on migration management, border governance, and internal security while promoting sustainable partnerships between EU Member States and partner nations. With a combined financial envelope of €14 million , the 2026 Calls for Proposals are open on a rolling basis , allowing eligible applicants to submit proposals until all available funds have been allocated. This flexible application model provides applicants with the opportunity to prepare strong project proposals while encouraging early submissions due to limited available funding. If your institution is involved in migration governance, border management, or international cooperation, this funding opportunity could support impactful projects that contribute to the implementation of the European Union Migration Policy s External Dimension. About the Migration Partnership Facility (MPF) The Migration Partnership Facility (MPF) is an initiative that supports the implementation of migration partnerships between European Union Member States and partner countries. The facility translates strategic priorities under the EU Migration Policy s External Dimension into practical projects through competitive grant funding. The programme enables eligible institutions to develop and implement migration-related initiatives that address shared migration challenges while fostering stronger international cooperation. Through its grant programme, the MPF finances projects that contribute to: Better migration governance Stronger partnerships between the EU and partner countries Improved border management systems Enhanced internal security cooperation Capacity development Sustainable migration solutions Knowledge sharing and institutional collaboration The Migration Partnership Facility serves as an important mechanism for transforming migration policy priorities into practical actions that generate measurable impact. 2026 Migration Partnership Facility Calls for Proposals The 2026 funding round includes three separate funding windows, each targeting a different strategic priority. 1. Call for Proposals 2026 – Migration Partnerships The Migration Partnerships Call aims to strengthen cooperation between EU Member States and partner countries through projects that improve migration governance and partnership implementation. Funding Available Financial envelope: €6,000,000 Funding Source: Asylum, Migration and Integration Fund (AMIF) Opening Date 13 July 2026 Deadline There is no fixed application deadline . Applications are accepted on a rolling basis until the available funding has been fully committed . Because funding is limited, applicants are encouraged to submit proposals as early as possible. 2. Call for Proposals 2026 – Border Management The Border Management Call focuses on strengthening border governance, improving migration management systems, and supporting projects that contribute to effective border administration. Funding Available Financial envelope: €5,000,000 Funding Source: Border Management and Visa Instrument (BMVI) Opening Date 13 July 2026 Deadline There is no closing date . Applications remain open on a rolling basis until the available funding has been exhausted. Early application is strongly recommended. 3. Call for Proposals 2026 – Internal Security The Internal Security Call supports initiatives that enhance cooperation in internal security while contributing to broader migration management objectives. Funding Available Financial envelope: €3,000,000 Funding Source: Internal Security Fund (ISF) Opening Date 13 July 2026 Deadline No fixed deadline has been established. Applications will continue to be reviewed and funded until the allocated budget has been fully utilized. Total Funding Available Across all three calls, the Migration Partnership Facility has allocated: Funding Window Financial Envelope Migration Partnerships €6,000,000 Border Management €5,000,000 Internal Security €3,000,000 Total Available Funding: €14,000,000 Objectives of the 2026 Calls The funding programme aims to support projects that contribute to implementing the European Union s external migration priorities by: Strengthening migration partnerships Promoting cooperation between EU Member States and partner countries Enhancing migration governance Supporting border management reforms Improving institutional capacities Advancing internal security cooperation Facilitating sustainable migration solutions Encouraging collaborative project implementation These objectives help ensure that migration is managed in a coordinated, secure, and mutually beneficial manner. Why This Funding Opportunity Matters Migration remains one of the European Union s major policy priorities. Effective migration governance requires close cooperation between countries of origin, transit, and destination. The Migration Partnership Facility provides practical financial support that enables governments and eligible institutions to transform strategic migration priorities into operational programmes. Through these grants, successful applicants can: Develop innovative migration management initiatives Strengthen institutional partnerships Improve border management systems Build technical and operational capacities Enhance regional cooperation Promote sustainable migration governance Support policy implementation Deliver measurable development outcomes Rolling Application Process Unlike many grant programmes that operate with a fixed deadline, the Migration Partnership Facility accepts applications on a continuous basis. This means: Applications can be submitted at any time. Proposals are reviewed as they are received. Funding is awarded while resources remain available. Once the allocated budget has been exhausted, the calls will close. Applicants are therefore encouraged to prepare and submit proposals early to maximize their chances of securing funding. Funding Sources The 2026 Calls are financed through three major European Union funding instruments: Asylum, Migration and Integration Fund (AMIF) Supports initiatives that improve migration management, integration, asylum systems, and international migration partnerships. Border Management and Visa Instrument (BMVI) Supports projects aimed at strengthening border management systems, visa policies, and external border cooperation. Internal Security Fund (ISF) Finances initiatives that enhance security cooperation, institutional resilience, and internal security capacities. How to Apply Eligible applicants should prepare project proposals that align with the objectives of the respective funding window. Applicants should: Review the relevant Call for Proposals. Ensure that their proposed project aligns with the funding priorities. Prepare all required documentation. Submit the proposal while funding remains available. For support or general enquiries regarding the Calls for Proposals, applicants may contact the Migration Partnership Facility via: Email: mpf@icmpd.org APPLY HERE Important Dates Call Opening Date: 13 July 2026 Application Deadline: No fixed deadline. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis until funds are fully allocated. Visit HERE to learn more about the Migration Partnership Facility 2026 Calls for Proposals. Key Highlights Up to €14 million available across three funding calls. Rolling applications with no fixed deadline. Three specialized funding windows. Supports implementation of the EU Migration Policy s External Dimension. Encourages cooperation between EU Member States and partner countries. Focus areas include migration partnerships, border management, and internal security. Projects are financed through AMIF, BMVI, and ISF. Early submission is encouraged due to limited funding. Conclusion The Migration Partnership Facility 2026 Calls for Proposals present a significant opportunity for eligible EU Member States to secure funding for projects that strengthen international migration cooperation, border governance, and internal security. With a total funding envelope of €14 million and a rolling application process, institutions have the flexibility to develop high-quality proposals while responding to evolving migration priorities. However, since funding will be awarded until available resources are exhausted, prospective applicants are strongly encouraged to submit their proposals as early as possible. Organizations capable of delivering impactful migration-related initiatives should take advantage of this opportunity to contribute to stronger international partnerships and more effective migration governance. For more grant opportunities visit OFY HERE.
