title: Digital Humanities Fellowship 2026/27 – Advocacy & Engagement Opportunity in the UK and Ireland
summary: Introduction The UK-Ireland Digital Humanities Association is pleased to announce the opening of applications for the 2026/27 Advocacy Engagement Fellowship , a prestigious opportunity designed to strengthen the advocacy strand of the Association’s activities and advance the theme of Openness and Transparency within the Digital Humanities community. This fellowship represents a significant investment in the future of Digital Humanities across the UK and Ireland, offering researchers, practitioners, and professionals the chance to contribute meaningfully to the evolving landscape of institutional and policy drivers that shape the discipline. Digital Humanities, as an interdisciplinary field, continues to expand its influence across academic institutions, cultural heritage organizations, and policy-making bodies. The need for effective advocacy has never been greater. As universities, libraries, archives, museums, and funding bodies grapple with questions of openness, transparency, and equitable access to knowledge, the role of advocacy becomes central to ensuring that Digital Humanities remains responsive, inclusive, and impactful. The Advocacy Engagement Fellowship is designed to address this need by appointing a dedicated fellow who will undertake research, stakeholder engagement, and community-building activities over a twelve-month period. This fellowship is not merely an appointment; it is a call to action. It invites individuals with a passion for Digital Humanities to step forward and help shape the discourse around openness and transparency. By engaging with stakeholders across sectors, developing value propositions, and contributing to best practice guidance, the fellow will play a pivotal role in ensuring that the Association’s advocacy efforts align with the evolving needs of the community. The fellowship also provides a platform for underrepresented voices, encouraging diversity and inclusivity in Digital Humanities advocacy. The 2026/27 Advocacy Engagement Fellowship is structured to provide flexibility, support, and recognition. With a remuneration package of £4,000, supplemented by £1,000 for fellowship-related activities, the fellow will be empowered to dedicate approximately ten hours per month to this work. The fellowship is designed to accommodate varying professional circumstances, allowing for adjustments in start and completion dates, and offering the possibility of joint applications for those who wish to share the role. Applications are invited from individuals resident in the UK or Ireland, with experience in research, digital practice, technical innovation, or cultural heritage. The Association particularly welcomes applications from those traditionally underrepresented in Digital Humanities, recognizing the importance of diverse perspectives in shaping advocacy strategies. The fellowship will commence in October 2026 , following a rigorous selection process that includes shortlisting in late August and interviews in early September. This article provides a comprehensive overview of the fellowship, including its objectives, responsibilities, funding arrangements, application process, and expected outputs. It also explores the broader significance of advocacy in Digital Humanities, the theme of openness and transparency, and the potential impact of the fellowship on the UK-Ireland Digital Humanities community. A detailed FAQ section is included to address common queries, ensuring that prospective applicants have access to all the information they need to prepare a strong application. Section 1: Fellowship Overview The Advocacy Engagement Fellowship is a cornerstone initiative of the UK-Ireland Digital Humanities Association. It is designed to advance the Association’s mission of fostering collaboration, innovation, and advocacy within the Digital Humanities community. The fellowship provides a structured yet flexible framework for individuals to contribute to the Association’s advocacy plan, focusing on the theme of Openness and Transparency for the 2026/27 cycle. Key Features of the Fellowship: Duration and Commitment Twelve months, commencing in October 2026. Approximately ten hours per month dedicated to fellowship activities. Flexibility in scheduling, with options for late start or early completion. Remuneration and Support £4,000 stipend, paid in three instalments. £1,000 additional support for fellowship-related expenses (travel, events, catering, etc.). Potential access to additional funds for attending key Digital Humanities events. Eligibility Applicants must be resident in the UK or Ireland. Open to researchers, digital practitioners, technical professionals, and GLAM sector professionals. Applications encouraged from underrepresented groups in Digital Humanities. Joint applications accepted for job-sharing arrangements. Responsibilities Undertake research into Digital Humanities in the UK and Ireland. Engage with stakeholders through surveys, interviews, focus groups, and workshops. Develop value propositions to support advocacy efforts. Contribute to community engagement around openness and transparency. Produce outputs such as reports, podcasts, videos, or other media, shared openly with the community. Theme: Openness and Transparency Projects should explore advocacy in relation to openness and transparency. Potential areas include cross-sector collaboration, policy-level advocacy, improving access to digital scholarship, and developing best practice guidance. Section 2: Theme – Openness and Transparency The 2026/27 Advocacy Engagement Fellowship is anchored in the theme of Openness and Transparency , a principle that lies at the very heart of contemporary Digital Humanities. This theme is not incidental; it reflects a deliberate choice by the UK-Ireland Digital Humanities Association to foreground values that are increasingly critical in academic, cultural, and policy contexts. By focusing on openness and transparency, the fellowship seeks to address pressing challenges in research culture, knowledge dissemination, and cross-sector collaboration, while also promoting inclusivity and accountability. 2.1 The Significance of Openness in Digital Humanities Openness in Digital Humanities encompasses a wide range of practices and commitments, including: Open Access to Scholarship : Ensuring that research outputs are freely available to the public, thereby democratizing access to knowledge and reducing barriers for researchers, practitioners, and communities outside traditional academic institutions. Open Data and Resources : Promoting the sharing of datasets, tools, and methodologies to enable replication, innovation, and collaborative research across disciplines and sectors. Open Collaboration : Encouraging partnerships between higher education institutions, cultural heritage organizations, technical professionals, and community groups to foster diverse perspectives and shared ownership of Digital Humanities projects. Open Pedagogy : Developing teaching and training resources that are accessible to a wide audience, thereby expanding the reach of Digital Humanities education and capacity-building. Openness is not merely a technical or logistical matter; it is a philosophical commitment to inclusivity, equity, and the democratization of knowledge. By embedding openness into advocacy strategies, the fellowship aims to ensure that Digital Humanities remains a field that is accessible, responsive, and relevant to a broad spectrum of stakeholders. 2.2 Transparency as a Core Value Transparency complements openness by emphasizing clarity, accountability, and integrity in research and advocacy practices. Within the context of Digital Humanities, transparency involves: Transparent Research Practices : Clearly articulating methodologies, assumptions, and limitations in research outputs to foster trust and credibility. Transparent Policy Engagement : Ensuring that advocacy efforts with funders, national bodies, and institutions are conducted openly, with clear communication of objectives, processes, and outcomes. Transparent Community Engagement : Building trust with stakeholders by maintaining open lines of communication, sharing progress and challenges, and inviting feedback throughout the fellowship. Transparent Evaluation and Reporting : Producing outputs that are not only accessible but also accompanied by documentation that explains how conclusions were reached and how recommendations can be implemented. Transparency is essential for building legitimacy in advocacy efforts. It reassures stakeholders that Digital Humanities is a field committed to ethical practices, rigorous standards, and accountability to the communities it serves. 2.3 The Fellowship’s Role in Advancing Openness and Transparency The Advocacy Engagement Fellow will play a pivotal role in operationalizing the theme of openness and transparency. This will involve: Mapping Practices Across the UK and Ireland Conducting desk research to identify existing practices of openness and transparency in Digital Humanities. Surveying the community to gather insights into challenges, opportunities, and best practices. Contextualizing differences between Ireland and the UK, particularly in relation to frameworks such as REF, UKRI, Research Ireland, and Impact 2030. Engaging Stakeholders Organizing interviews, focus groups, and workshops to facilitate dialogue around openness and transparency. Building cross-sector partnerships with non-HEI organizations and communities to expand the reach of Digital Humanities advocacy. Developing Value Propositions Creating clear, evidence-based arguments that demonstrate the value of openness and transparency in Digital Humanities. Providing researchers with tools to articulate the significance of their work in policy and funding contexts. Producing Outputs Generating reports, podcasts, videos, or other media that document findings and recommendations. Ensuring that all outputs are shared openly with the Digital Humanities community, thereby embodying the principles of openness and transparency. 2.4 Potential Areas of Exploration The fellowship invites projects that explore openness and transparency in diverse ways. Potential areas include: Cross-Sector Collaboration : Developing best practice guidance, collaborative tools, or training programs to support partnerships between academia and non-HEI organizations. Research Culture Improvement : Investigating how openness and transparency can enhance research culture, particularly by addressing differences in practices between Ireland and the UK. Public Access to Scholarship : Identifying barriers to open access and proposing strategies to improve public engagement with digital scholarship. Policy-Level Advocacy : Crafting value propositions that highlight the importance of Digital Humanities in policy and funding contexts, thereby strengthening the field’s position in national and institutional agendas. 2.5 Broader Impact of the Theme By centering the fellowship on openness and transparency, the UK-Ireland Digital Humanities Association is making a strategic statement about the future of the field. The fellowship is not only about individual outputs; it is about shaping a culture of advocacy that prioritizes inclusivity, accountability, and accessibility. The impact of this theme will extend beyond the fellowship year, influencing how Digital Humanities is practiced, taught, and valued across the UK and Ireland. Section 3: Eligibility and Qualifications The 2026/27 Advocacy Engagement Fellowship is open to a wide range of applicants, reflecting the interdisciplinary and cross-sector nature of Digital Humanities. The Association recognizes that advocacy requires diverse perspectives, and therefore encourages applications from individuals across different professional and academic backgrounds. 3.1 Residency Requirement Applicants must be resident in the United Kingdom or Ireland . This requirement ensures that fellows are embedded within the regional context of the Association’s work, enabling them to engage directly with stakeholders and communities in both countries. 3.2 Professional Backgrounds Applications are welcomed from individuals with experience in: Academic Research : Scholars conducting research in Digital Humanities or related fields. Digital Practitioners : Professionals engaged in digital projects, tool development, or digital scholarship. Technical Professionals : Individuals with expertise in computing, data management, or technical infrastructure relevant to Digital Humanities. GLAM Sector Professionals : Staff from galleries, libraries, archives, and museums who are interested in expanding their role within the Digital Humanities community. 3.3 Diversity and Inclusion The Association particularly encourages applications from those traditionally underrepresented in Digital Humanities. Diversity is seen as a strength, and the fellowship aims to amplify voices that have historically been marginalized in academic and cultural contexts. 3.4 Joint Applications The fellowship allows for job-sharing arrangements , enabling two individuals to apply jointly. Joint applicants must submit a single application form and statement of interest, but provide individual CVs and letters of support. 3.5 Letters of Support Applicants who are currently enrolled as students or employed by an organization must provide a letter of support from their manager or academic supervisor. This letter should acknowledge that approximately ten hours per month will be dedicated to fellowship activities. Section 4: Fellowship Responsibilities and Outputs The Advocacy Engagement Fellow will undertake a range of responsibilities designed to advance the Association’s advocacy plan. These responsibilities are structured to ensure that the fellowship produces tangible outputs while also fostering community engagement. 4.1 Research Activities Desk Research : Reviewing existing literature, policies, and practices related to openness and transparency in Digital Humanities. Community Surveys : Designing and administering surveys to gather insights from the Digital Humanities community. Stakeholder Engagement : Conducting interviews, focus groups, and workshops with key stakeholders. 4.2 Value Proposition Development Based on research and engagement activities, the fellow will develop a set of value propositions that articulate the significance of Digital Humanities in policy and funding contexts. These propositions will serve as tools for researchers and practitioners to advocate for their work. 4.3 Community Engagement The fellow will contribute to wider community engagement around advocacy, openness, and transparency. This may include organizing sessions at in-person events, contributing to regional meetings, and producing accessible outputs. 4.4 Outputs The fellowship requires the production of outputs that are shared openly with the community. These may include: Written reports. Podcasts. Videos. Other media forms. All outputs must be accompanied by supporting documentation and a proposed implementation plan. Section 5: Value, Duration, and Funding 5.1 Duration The fellowship will last for 12 months , commencing in October 2026 . Exact start and completion dates can be adjusted to accommodate the fellow’s circumstances. 5.2 Time Commitment Approximately 10 hours per month . Flexible scheduling to allow fellows to balance other professional or academic commitments. 5.3 Remuneration £4,000 stipend , paid in three instalments. Payment can be made directly to the fellow or to their employing organization as a buyout. 5.4 Additional Support £1,000 to support fellowship activities (travel, catering, event expenses). Potential access to additional funds for attending key Digital Humanities events, subject to approval. Section 6: Application Process 6.1 Required Materials Applicants must submit the following: Application Form (including contact details for a reference). Curriculum Vitae (maximum 2 pages). Proposal (maximum 1,000 words) outlining interest, research area, and intended outputs. Implementation Plan (maximum 500 words), optionally supplemented by a Gantt chart. Letter of Support (if applicable). Equality and Diversity Form (optional). 6.2 Submission All materials must be submitted as PDFs to: uk-ie.digitalhumanities@sas.ac.uk . 6.3 Deadlines Application deadline : Monday, 17 August 2026 at 23:59 BST . Shortlisting : Week commencing 31 August 2026 . Interviews : Week commencing 7 September 2026 . Fellowship start : Early October 2026. Section 7: Key Dates and Timeline Application Deadline : 17 August 2026. Shortlisting : 31 August 2026. Interviews : 7 September 2026. Commencement : October 2026. Send your application to uk-ie.digitalhumanities@sas.ac.uk today! Section 8: Potential Research Areas and Projects Examples of potential projects include: Developing best practice guidance for cross-sector partnerships. Contextualizing differences in research practices between Ireland and the UK. Improving public and open access to digital scholarship. Creating value propositions for Digital Humanities in policy contexts. Section 9: Benefits of Participation Opportunity to shape advocacy strategies in Digital Humanities. Engagement with leading stakeholders across the UK and Ireland. Professional recognition and financial support. Contribution to a theme of openness and transparency that will influence the field for years to come. Section 10: Broader Impact on Digital Humanities The fellowship is expected to have a lasting impact by: Strengthening advocacy for Digital Humanities. Promoting openness and transparency as core values. Enhancing collaboration across sectors. Supporting diversity and inclusion in the field. Section 11: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) 11.1 General Questions What is the purpose of the fellowship? To advance advocacy in Digital Humanities, focusing on openness and transparency. Who can apply? Residents of the UK or Ireland with relevant experience in research, digital practice, technical work, or GLAM sectors. Is joint application allowed? Yes, two individuals may apply together. What is the time commitment? Approximately 10 hours per month. What is the stipend? £4,000, plus £1,000 for fellowship activities. 11.2 Application Questions What documents are required? Application form, CV, proposal, implementation plan, letter of support (if applicable), and optional equality and diversity form. How should applications be submitted? As PDFs to uk-ie.digitalhumanities@sas.ac.uk. What is the deadline? 17 August 2026 at 23:59 BST. When will interviews take place? Week commencing 7 September 2026. When does the fellowship start? Early October 2026. 11.3 Fellowship Activities What kind of research will the fellow undertake? Desk research, surveys, stakeholder engagement, and workshops. What outputs are expected? Reports, podcasts, videos, or other media, shared openly with the community. Will the fellow attend events? Yes, including regional meetings and potentially other key Digital Humanities events. Is flexibility allowed in scheduling? Yes, adjustments can be made to start and completion dates. Can students apply? Yes, with a letter of support from their supervisor. To learn more about the Digital Humanities Fellowship 2026/27, click HERE . Conclusion The 2026/27 Advocacy Engagement Fellowship represents a unique opportunity to contribute to the advancement of Digital Humanities in the UK and Ireland. By focusing on the theme of Openness and Transparency , the fellowship underscores the Association’s commitment to inclusivity, accountability, and accessibility. The appointed fellow will not only undertake research and stakeholder engagement but also produce outputs that will shape advocacy strategies for years to come. With financial support, flexibility, and a clear mandate, the fellowship offers an invaluable platform for individuals passionate about Digital Humanities to make a lasting impact. title: RWJF Health Policy Fellows Program: Fully Immersive Leadership Fellowship for Mid-Career Professionals to Shape U.S. Health Policy
summary: Health policy decisions influence the quality of healthcare systems, determine access to essential medical services, and shape the health outcomes of millions of people. For experienced professionals seeking to move beyond research, clinical practice, or public service into the heart of policymaking, the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation (RWJF) Health Policy Fellows Program provides one of the most prestigious opportunities available. The RWJF Health Policy Fellows Program is a highly respected, nonpartisan leadership fellowship designed specifically for accomplished mid-career professionals who wish to gain firsthand experience in the U.S. federal policymaking process. Through an immersive year-long placement in Washington, DC, fellows work directly alongside members of Congress, congressional committees, or executive branch agencies while contributing to policies that improve health and healthcare across the United States. Since its establishment in 1973, the fellowship has prepared more than 300 influential leaders who have gone on to shape health policy, strengthen healthcare systems, and influence national conversations on public health and healthcare reform. This fellowship offers an exceptional combination of policy education, leadership development, practical government experience, strategic communications training, and access to an influential network of policymakers and health leaders. About the RWJF Health Policy Fellows Program The RWJF Health Policy Fellows Program provides experienced professionals with an extraordinary opportunity to bridge the gap between technical expertise and policymaking. Participants spend one full year immersed in the federal policy environment, learning how legislation is developed, how executive agencies shape national health priorities, and how evidence is translated into public policy. Rather than remaining observers, fellows become active participants in federal decision-making. During the fellowship, participants gain practical experience by contributing directly to the work of policymakers and government officials responsible for shaping America s health system. The program equips fellows with: Advanced leadership skills Practical policymaking experience Legislative knowledge Executive branch exposure Strategic communication abilities High-level networking opportunities Long-term professional connections The fellowship is administered in collaboration with the National Academy of Medicine (NAM), ensuring participants receive world-class policy education and mentorship. Why This Fellowship Matters Many experienced professionals possess deep technical expertise but have limited exposure to how federal policies are actually created. The RWJF Health Policy Fellows Program closes that gap by allowing fellows to experience policymaking from the inside. Participants develop a comprehensive understanding of: Federal legislative processes Executive branch policymaking Congressional operations Health policy development Budget negotiations Stakeholder engagement National healthcare priorities This experience enables graduates to become stronger leaders capable of influencing healthcare systems at institutional, state, and national levels. Fellowship Structure The fellowship is divided into several major phases designed to maximize both learning and practical experience. Phase 1: Intensive Orientation The fellowship officially begins in September with an intensive three-and-a-half-month orientation organized by the National Academy of Medicine. During this period, fellows receive comprehensive preparation before entering government placements. The orientation includes meetings with: National health leaders Members of Congress Congressional staff Executive branch officials Think tanks Advocacy organizations Policy experts Interest groups Participants also attend seminars covering topics such as: Health economics Federal healthcare financing Congressional budget processes Current health policy priorities Federal legislative procedures Executive decision-making Health policy analysis This orientation prepares fellows to contribute immediately once they begin their placements. Phase 2: Federal Government Placement Most fellowship placements begin in January . Each fellow joins either: A congressional office A congressional committee An executive branch agency Rather than serving as observers, fellows become full members of policy teams under the mentorship of experienced senior staff members. Throughout the placement, fellows actively contribute to policy development and legislative activities. Typical responsibilities include: Policy Development Fellows help: Develop policy proposals Analyze health legislation Recommend policy positions Conduct policy research Legislative Drafting Participants assist in: Drafting legislation Preparing policy amendments Writing legislative summaries Policy Communications Fellows prepare: Briefing documents Policy memos Background papers Research summaries Congressional Engagement Participants organize: Congressional hearings Stakeholder briefings Policy discussions Committee meetings Stakeholder Relations Fellows engage with: Constituents Advocacy organizations Healthcare providers Government agencies Professional associations Senior Briefings Participants frequently brief: Members of Congress Congressional staff Executive officials Senior policymakers This direct exposure allows fellows to understand how national health policies move from concept to implementation. Additional Leadership Development The learning experience extends well beyond the workplace. Throughout the fellowship year, participants continue attending nonpartisan seminars covering emerging health policy issues. Additional professional development opportunities include: Leadership workshops Strategic communications training Media engagement training Group policy discussions Professional networking events National Academy of Medicine meetings Each fellow also prepares a formal presentation addressing a health policy issue encountered during the fellowship. These presentations strengthen analytical, communication, and leadership skills. Fellowship Extension Opportunity Although the standard fellowship lasts from September 1 through August 31 , fellows may request approval from the National Program Office to remain in Washington beyond the official residential period. Approved extensions may continue: Through the legislative session Until December 31 This provides additional opportunities for policy engagement and project completion. Alumni Network Completion of the fellowship marks the beginning—not the end—of long-term engagement. Graduates become members of a nationwide alumni community consisting of distinguished health leaders. Many alumni return annually to Washington, DC, for: Alumni retreats Health policy briefings Professional networking Leadership discussions The alumni network provides continued opportunities for collaboration throughout participants careers. Eligibility Requirements The fellowship seeks exceptional professionals with substantial expertise and demonstrated leadership potential. Applicants must satisfy several eligibility requirements. Professional Background Applicants should currently work within: Academic institutions Non-profit organizations Government agencies Military services U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs U.S. Public Health Service Commissioned Corps Eligible state government offices Federal, tribal, state, and local government employees may apply provided they are not classified as government officials under Section 4946 of the Internal Revenue Code. Educational Requirements Applicants must possess: A master s degree; or A doctoral degree Advanced degrees should relate to a health-related discipline or an area contributing to health policy. Professional Expertise Applicants must possess significant expertise in a health-related field. Examples include: Medicine Nursing Public health Law Dentistry Economics Social sciences Housing policy Transportation Nutrition Wealth and economic policy Employment Education Environmental health Community development Health services research Social work Behavioral health Other health professions Professionals whose work addresses broader determinants of health are also encouraged to apply. Ineligible Applicants The following individuals are not eligible: Professionals whose primary responsibilities involve government relations Individuals whose primary work focuses on advocacy Applicants related by blood or marriage to officers or trustees of the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation Descendants of Robert Wood Johnson Citizenship Requirement Applicants must be either: U.S. citizens; or U.S. permanent residents Eligibility is determined at the time of application. Because fellows work within the federal government, future policy or legal changes could affect fellowship eligibility or placement conditions. Selection Process The fellowship uses a rigorous, competitive selection process. Initial Application Review Applications are evaluated by the advisory board using several leadership and professional criteria. Finalist Selection By mid-January , finalists are selected and invited for interviews. Interviews Finalists participate in in-person interviews in Washington, DC during March . Interview invitations include additional information regarding the remainder of the selection process. Selection Criteria Applicants are assessed based on several important qualities. These include: Outstanding professional accomplishments Leadership potential in health policy Career growth potential Ability to improve health outcomes nationally Communication skills Interpersonal effectiveness Vision for applying fellowship experience to future career goals Characteristics of Successful Candidates The fellowship seeks individuals who have already demonstrated excellence within their profession. Ideal candidates typically: Are recognized leaders in their field Demonstrate professional credibility Show commitment to improving health systems Think strategically Adapt quickly to changing environments Collaborate effectively Learn rapidly Exhibit emotional intelligence Build strong professional relationships Communicate clearly Exercise discretion Display patience and humility Approach challenges with curiosity and critical thinking The program also strongly encourages applicants from professional disciplines that have historically been underrepresented within the fellowship to apply. Diverse professional experiences, perspectives, and career pathways are viewed as strengths. Benefits of the RWJF Health Policy Fellows Program Participants receive numerous professional and leadership benefits, including: Immersive federal government policy experience Hands-on legislative and executive branch work Intensive policy education Leadership development Strategic communications training Mentorship from experienced policymakers National Academy of Medicine engagement Access to influential national health leaders Long-term alumni network Enhanced leadership credibility Expanded professional network Practical experience influencing national health policy Why You Should Apply If you are an accomplished health professional who wants to influence healthcare beyond clinical practice, research, or administration, this fellowship offers a rare opportunity to participate directly in national policymaking. Graduates leave with practical legislative experience, stronger leadership skills, broader professional networks, and a deeper understanding of how federal decisions shape healthcare across the nation. The experience prepares fellows to become influential leaders capable of advancing meaningful and lasting improvements in health policy. APPLY HERE Deadline At the time of the provided information, no application deadline has been specified . Interested applicants should monitor the official fellowship webpage for application opening and closing dates. Visit HERE to learn more about the RWJF Health Policy Fellows Program. Conclusion The RWJF Health Policy Fellows Program stands among the most prestigious leadership fellowships available for experienced health professionals in the United States. Through an intensive orientation, hands-on placements in Congress or the executive branch, leadership development, policy training, and lifelong alumni engagement, the program equips fellows with the knowledge, experience, and networks needed to influence health policy at the highest levels. For mid-career professionals committed to improving health outcomes and shaping the future of healthcare, this fellowship provides an unparalleled platform to turn expertise into lasting national impact.
